revenueModel._note: Five system terms plus Installed Base Management. Metrology and Inspection is a direct term: it is system sales but not lithography, and no unit count is disclosed. cashPolicy.source: default: all cash treated as excess, pending an operating/excess split from /collect (open item E3)
cashPolicy._note: Operating cash = revenue * operatingCashPctRevenue. It sits inside OWC and therefore inside invested capital. The remainder is excess cash and is netted against longTermDebt in the valuation bridge. At 0.0 the bridge is arithmetically identical to SKILL section 2 (netDebt = longTermDebt - operatingCash), so no per-share number moves; only invested capital, ROIC and EVA change. This is the resolution of open item X1.

otherOpAssetsModel.nonScalingStockSource: FY2024 US GAAP consolidated balance sheet, non-current assets: goodwill 4,588.6 + other intangible assets net 621.3 + equity method investments 903.0 = 6,112.9. Tight split: only balances that do not move with revenue. Reconciliation: total non-current assets 17,852.2 less PPE 6,846.8 = 11,005.4, equal to the model line and to the sum of the eight components. Corroboration: independent OLS of otherOperatingAssets on revenue FY2020-24 gives an intercept of 6,757.9, within 9.5 percent of this composed figure. Behaviour check: this bucket moved -137.0 in FY2024 (goodwill flat, intangibles amortising, equity method flat), which is how a fixed stock behaves. Deferred tax (1,940.7) and loans receivable (1,456.6) were deliberately EXCLUDED: together they grew +458.8 in FY2024 alone, so freezing them would assume that growth stops. VALIDATED ON FIVE YEARS in v0.9: the tight stock runs 6,499 / 6,401 / 6,322 / 6,251 / 6,113 across FY2020-FY2024, down 5.9 percent while revenue rose 102 percent. A fixed stock, confirmed.
otherOpAssetsModel._note: Under stock_plus_ratio, otherOperatingAssets = nonScalingStock + revenue * driver. nonScalingStock is the portion of the FY2024 balance of 11,005.4 that does not scale with revenue (goodwill, intangibles, equity investments, deferred tax and similar), in model units. The driver then carries only the scaling remainder. Fall back to kind=flat if the split is not to hand: that holds the whole line constant, avoids the error, and gives up the operating portion's genuine scaling.

discount.source: WACC 0.10 from assumptions.wacc in evals/case-01/expected.json, the founder's hand-verified ASML SAMPLE. NO BAND: low = mid = high, because the W1 market band construction was never delivered. Per STATE.md the first /collect session (sesn_01L6DpzzsFsCnEXSsTETRsX6) was interrupted to stop token spend and no deliverables were fetched. A completed run supplies the band; a band has NOT been invented here. Consequence: the WACC line in the tornado has zero span by construction, exactly as the six anchored drivers do (O7). Terminal growth 0.02: the ECB medium-term inflation target, i.e. zero long-run real growth. No company-specific basis exists in this file. C5 (WACC across cases) settled as: one rate across bear, base and bull, so risk is not double-counted in both the cash flows and the discount rate. Moot while there is no band. C6 (discounting timing) settled as: end-year. Mid-year would raise every case by roughly half a year of discounting and is the more accurate treatment for cash arriving through the year; end-year is retained because SKILL section 2 does not specify and it is the lower number.
discount._note_waccByCase: Empty means the W1 mid band is held constant across bear/base/bull and WACC is swung only in the tornado. To couple the rate to the case instead, set {"bear":"waccHigh","base":"waccMid","bull":"waccLow"} and record the reason (unresolved convention C5).
discount._note_terminal: Set terminalMethod to fade_then_gordon and fadeYears > 0 to fade the final explicit growth rate down to terminalGrowth before capitalising.

netDebt._note: OPTIONAL OVERRIDE. Leave value null and the engine derives net debt as longTermDebt minus excess cash, where excess cash follows drivers.cashPolicy. Nulls here do not block.

sources.gross_margin_pct: ASML Investor Day, November 2024, 2030 model: total net sales of approximately 44 to 60bn at a gross margin of approximately 56 to 60 percent. Restated in the 2024 fourth-quarter and full-year Investor Relations presentation, filed with the SEC as exhibit 99.2 to a Form 6-K on 29 January 2025. BASIS CONVERSION, load-bearing: the Investor Day figure is a REPORTED gross margin; this driver is a HOUSE gross margin, which excludes production depreciation because schema-v2 states depreciation on its own line. FY2024 reported 51.28 percent, house 53.05 percent, wedge 1.77pp (production depreciation 501.5 on revenue 28,262.9). House-basis 2030 targets are therefore 57.77 / 59.77 / 61.77 percent, not 56 / 58 / 60. Applying the guidance unconverted would understate the driver by 1.77pp. RULE: linear interpolation from the FY2024 house actual of 53.05 percent to the house-basis 2030 target over six steps; the model horizon takes the first five. REVISABLE: margin expansion driven by High-NA mix, volume leverage and Installed Base Management growth will not be a straight line. CASE COUPLING: bear takes the low end, bull the high, matching how the Investor Day pairs its revenue and margin scenarios. The revenue tree must later be built to the matching revenue bracket (44 / 52 / 60bn) or the cases become internally inconsistent. CONSERVATIVE IN TWO PLACES: the wedge is held constant at 1.77pp, but capex near 7.9 percent of revenue against depreciation near 3.2 percent means depreciation-to-revenue rises and the wedge widens, so the true house target is above these figures; and the terminal value capitalises from FY2029, before the 2030 target is reached.
sources.opex_pct_revenue: FY2022-FY2024 anchor window (O2: FY2020-21 excluded). Shape: level (18.77, 17.39, 17.90; range 1.38pp). Rule: three-year mean held flat. Covers R&D plus SG&A combined, since schema-v2 has no R&D line. R&D is committed and does not flex with shipments, so this ratio rises in a downcycle. Bear, base and bull are IDENTICAL for this driver. The anchor window contains no downcycle, so the observed range understates the true spread and no spread has been invented. Widen from a longer history (FY2012-13, FY2019) or Investor Day 2030 guidance before stamping.
sources.dep_pct_prior_ppe: FY2022-FY2024 anchor window (O2: FY2020-21 excluded). Shape: trend, down (19.46, 18.59, 16.63; decrements -0.87 then -1.96pp). The decline is mechanical: capex near 8 percent of rising revenue grows PPE faster than depreciation follows, and the ratio should asymptote toward the inverse of average useful life. Rule: hold the FY2024 actual flat, because continuing the trend needs a PPE-growth and asset-life view that is not in this file. Denominated in prior PPE rather than revenue, so it is case-independent and carries one path across all three cases by design, not by omission.
sources.capex_incl_pct_revenue: FY2022-FY2024 anchor window (O2: FY2020-21 excluded). Shape: level (7.28, 8.28, 8.02; range 1.00pp). Rule: three-year mean held flat. House capex is delta(net PPE) plus depreciation. Capex is committed one to two years out, so this ratio rises when revenue falls. Bear, base and bull are IDENTICAL for this driver. The anchor window contains no downcycle, so the observed range understates the true spread and no spread has been invented. Widen from a longer history (FY2012-13, FY2019) or Investor Day 2030 guidance before stamping.
sources.owc_pct_revenue: FY2022-FY2024 anchor window (O2: FY2020-21 excluded). Shape: swing, not level (-6.80, +4.04, -3.68; range 10.84pp on 28.3bn of revenue, i.e. 1.4 to 3bn of FOCF). Rule per O3: three-year mean held flat, with the swing belonging in the tornado rather than in a point estimate. Filled from the POLICY column of the anchor sheet, not the legacy column: under a 0.0 cash policy, cash is excess and does not scale with revenue. Customer prepayments in otherNonInterestLiab are the swing: strong bookings push OWC more negative, a downcycle drains them. Bear, base and bull are IDENTICAL for this driver. The anchor window contains no downcycle, so the observed range understates the true spread and no spread has been invented. Widen from a longer history (FY2012-13, FY2019) or Investor Day 2030 guidance before stamping.
sources.tax_rate: FY2022-FY2024 anchor window (O2: FY2020-21 excluded). Shape: trend, up (15.02, 15.81, 18.59). Per open item T1 this is the IMPLIED EFFECTIVE rate from the income lines, NOT assumptions.taxRate of 0.2580, which is near the Dutch statutory rate and overstates tax by roughly 650 per year on FY2024 EBIT. Rule: hold the FY2024 implied rate flat. The climb is consistent with a 15 percent global minimum floor phasing in; if it continues toward statutory, value falls. Case-independent, so one path across all three cases by design.
sources.other_op_assets_scaling_pct_revenue: FY2020-FY2024, five years of component data from the yearly balance sheet in the source deck. Scaling remainder as a share of revenue: 16.94, 14.28, 14.03, 13.86, 17.31. Rule: FY2022-FY2024 mean per O2, held flat, with the range going to the tornado. Same treatment as owc_pct_revenue. SUPERSEDES the v0.5 fill of 17.31 percent, which held the FY2024 level flat when only FY2023 and FY2024 were visible; five years show FY2024 is the top of the range, elevated by the loans receivable step that remains unexplained under O4. Identical across bear, base and bull.

sources.gross_margin_pct: ASML Investor Day, November 2024, 2030 model: total net sales of approximately 44 to 60bn at a gross margin of approximately 56 to 60 percent. Restated in the 2024 fourth-quarter and full-year Investor Relations presentation, filed with the SEC as exhibit 99.2 to a Form 6-K on 29 January 2025. BASIS CONVERSION, load-bearing: the Investor Day figure is a REPORTED gross margin; this driver is a HOUSE gross margin, which excludes production depreciation because schema-v2 states depreciation on its own line. FY2024 reported 51.28 percent, house 53.05 percent, wedge 1.77pp (production depreciation 501.5 on revenue 28,262.9). House-basis 2030 targets are therefore 57.77 / 59.77 / 61.77 percent, not 56 / 58 / 60. Applying the guidance unconverted would understate the driver by 1.77pp. RULE: linear interpolation from the FY2024 house actual of 53.05 percent to the house-basis 2030 target over six steps; the model horizon takes the first five. REVISABLE: margin expansion driven by High-NA mix, volume leverage and Installed Base Management growth will not be a straight line. CASE COUPLING: bear takes the low end, bull the high, matching how the Investor Day pairs its revenue and margin scenarios. The revenue tree must later be built to the matching revenue bracket (44 / 52 / 60bn) or the cases become internally inconsistent. CONSERVATIVE IN TWO PLACES: the wedge is held constant at 1.77pp, but capex near 7.9 percent of revenue against depreciation near 3.2 percent means depreciation-to-revenue rises and the wedge widens, so the true house target is above these figures; and the terminal value capitalises from FY2029, before the 2030 target is reached.
sources.opex_pct_revenue: FY2022-FY2024 anchor window (O2: FY2020-21 excluded). Shape: level (18.77, 17.39, 17.90; range 1.38pp). Rule: three-year mean held flat. Covers R&D plus SG&A combined, since schema-v2 has no R&D line. R&D is committed and does not flex with shipments, so this ratio rises in a downcycle. Bear, base and bull are IDENTICAL for this driver. The anchor window contains no downcycle, so the observed range understates the true spread and no spread has been invented. Widen from a longer history (FY2012-13, FY2019) or Investor Day 2030 guidance before stamping.
sources.dep_pct_prior_ppe: FY2022-FY2024 anchor window (O2: FY2020-21 excluded). Shape: trend, down (19.46, 18.59, 16.63; decrements -0.87 then -1.96pp). The decline is mechanical: capex near 8 percent of rising revenue grows PPE faster than depreciation follows, and the ratio should asymptote toward the inverse of average useful life. Rule: hold the FY2024 actual flat, because continuing the trend needs a PPE-growth and asset-life view that is not in this file. Denominated in prior PPE rather than revenue, so it is case-independent and carries one path across all three cases by design, not by omission.
sources.capex_incl_pct_revenue: FY2022-FY2024 anchor window (O2: FY2020-21 excluded). Shape: level (7.28, 8.28, 8.02; range 1.00pp). Rule: three-year mean held flat. House capex is delta(net PPE) plus depreciation. Capex is committed one to two years out, so this ratio rises when revenue falls. Bear, base and bull are IDENTICAL for this driver. The anchor window contains no downcycle, so the observed range understates the true spread and no spread has been invented. sources.owc_pct_revenue: FY2022-FY2024 anchor window (O2: FY2020-21 excluded). Shape: swing, not level (-6.80, +4.04, -3.68; range 10.84pp on 28.3bn of revenue, i.e. 1.4 to 3bn of FOCF). Rule per O3: three-year mean held flat, with the swing belonging in the tornado rather than in a point estimate. Filled from the POLICY column of the anchor sheet, not the legacy column: under a 0.0 cash policy, cash is excess and does not scale with revenue. Customer prepayments in otherNonInterestLiab are the swing: strong bookings push OWC more negative, a downcycle drains them. Bear, base and bull are IDENTICAL for this driver. sources.tax_rate: FY2022-FY2024 anchor window (O2: FY2020-21 excluded). Shape: trend, up (15.02, 15.81, 18.59). Per open item T1 this is the IMPLIED EFFECTIVE rate from the income lines, NOT assumptions.taxRate of 0.2580, which is near the Dutch statutory rate and overstates tax by roughly 650 per year on FY2024 EBIT. sources.other_op_assets_scaling_pct_revenue: FY2020-FY2024, five years of component data from the yearly balance sheet in the source deck. sources.gross_margin_pct: ASML Investor Day, November 2024, 2030 model: total net sales of approximately 44 to 60bn at a gross margin of approximately 56 to 60 percent. Restated in the 2024 fourth-quarter and full-year Investor Relations presentation, filed with the SEC as exhibit 99.2 to a Form 6-K on 29 January 2025. BASIS CONVERSION, load-bearing: the Investor Day figure is a REPORTED gross margin; this driver is a HOUSE gross margin, which excludes production depreciation because schema-v2 states depreciation on its own line. FY2024 reported 51.28 percent, house 53.05 percent, wedge 1.77pp (production depreciation 501.5 on revenue 28,262.9). House-basis 2030 targets are therefore 57.77 / 59.77 / 61.77 percent, not 56 / 58 / 60. Applying the guidance unconverted would understate the driver by 1.77pp. RULE: linear interpolation from the FY2024 house actual of 53.05 percent to the house-basis 2030 target over six steps; the model horizon takes the first five. REVISABLE: margin expansion driven by High-NA mix, volume leverage and Installed Base Management growth will not be a straight line. CASE COUPLING: bear takes the low end, bull the high, matching how the Investor Day pairs its revenue and margin scenarios. The revenue tree must later be built to the matching revenue bracket (44 / 52 / 60bn) or the cases become internally inconsistent. CONSERVATIVE IN TWO PLACES: the wedge is held constant at 1.77pp, but capex near 7.9 percent of revenue against depreciation near 3.2 percent means depreciation-to-revenue rises and the wedge widens, so the true house target is above these figures; and the terminal value capitalises from FY2029, before the 2030 target is reached.
sources.opex_pct_revenue: FY2022-FY2024 anchor window (O2: FY2020-21 excluded). Shape: level (18.77, 17.39, 17.90; range 1.38pp). Rule: three-year mean held flat. Covers R&D plus SG&A combined, since schema-v2 has no R&D line. R&D is committed and does not flex with shipments, so this ratio rises in a downcycle. Bear, base and bull are IDENTICAL for this driver. The anchor window contains no downcycle, so the observed range understates the true spread and no spread has been invented. Widen from a longer history (FY2012-13, FY2019) or Investor Day 2030 guidance before stamping.
sources.dep_pct_prior_ppe: FY2022-FY2024 anchor window (O2: FY2020-21 excluded). Shape: trend, down (19.46, 18.59, 16.63; decrements -0.87 then -1.96pp). The decline is mechanical: capex near 8 percent of rising revenue grows PPE faster than depreciation follows, and the ratio should asymptote toward the inverse of average useful life. Rule: hold the FY2024 actual flat, because continuing the trend needs a PPE-growth and asset-life view that is not in this file. Denominated in prior PPE rather than revenue, so it is case-independent and carries one path across all three cases by design, not by omission.

The anchor window contains no downcycle, so the observed range understates the true spread and no spread has been invented.
